Re-homed from the BDK-343 btc-prague branch, where deck_settings_v1 lived in bmc-widget-protocol and was bound by a settings widget. Here it is a standalone protocol bound by the settings-tray layer-shell overlay. The dismiss request is dropped: hide is owned by deck_screen_edge_v1.

interface.name: deck_settings_v1
interface.description: Lightweight compositor-relayed IPC for the settings-tray overlay to control system state it must not touch directly. The target platform (OpenWrt/ARMv7) has no D-Bus/PipeWire/UPower; bmc owns the hardware drivers, so the overlay relays control through the compositor's Wayland connection. Only the settings-tray overlay binds this interface.

request.name: set_brightness
request.description: Request a display brightness change. Value is 0-100. bmc applies it night-mode-aware and reports the effective value back via brightness.

request.name: reconfigure_wifi
request.description: Request the compositor to put the device into WiFi setup mode: an open access point plus captive portal, the same flow used for factory-default setup. One-way; the device leaves setup mode on its own once a network is configured from the phone. Progress is reported via wifi_ap.

event.name: brightness
event.description: Report the effective display brightness. Emitted once when the overlay binds, and again whenever the effective brightness changes, including the night-mode value while night mode is active. Value is 0-100.

event.name: wifi_ap
event.description: Report the WiFi setup access-point SSID. A non-empty SSID means setup mode is active and the user can join this network from their phone; an empty string means setup mode is inactive. Emitted once on bind and again whenever the setup state changes.

arg.name: ssid
arg.summary: setup AP SSID, empty when inactive

enum.name: capability

description.summary: optional control surfaces this compositor supports

enum.description: Which controls the overlay should offer. Computed statically from the hardware product; a control whose bit is unset has no backing hardware or firmware path on this device.

request.name: set_volume
request.description: Request a sound volume change. Value is 0-100; 0 is mute. bmc applies it night-mode-aware (to the night config while night mode is active, else the day config) and reports the effective value back via volume.

request.name: toggle_night_mode
request.description: Toggle night mode with override semantics: outside the scheduled window the toggle forces night mode on/off until the next schedule boundary. The resulting state is reported via night_mode.

request.name: restart
request.description: Request a device reboot. bmc may decline (e.g. while a firmware upgrade is in progress), reported via restart_declined. On success no event arrives; the device reboots.

event.name: capabilities
event.description: Which optional controls this compositor supports. Emitted exactly once per resource, as the first event on bind, and static for the compositor's lifetime.

event.name: volume
event.description: Report the effective sound volume. Emitted once when the overlay binds (only on compositors with the sound capability, once bmc has reported a real value) and again whenever the effective volume changes, including the night-mode value while night mode is active. Value is 0-100.

event.name: night_mode
event.description: Report the night mode state. active is 1 while night mode is active, else 0. until is the "HH:MM" boundary the current state lasts to (the schedule end while active, the schedule start while enabled but inactive), or null while night mode is disabled. Emitted on bind once known and again on every change, including schedule edits.

event.name: restart_declined
event.description: One-shot notification that a restart request was not honored, with a short human-readable reason. Not state: never replayed on bind.

event.name: preempted

description.summary: a modal overlay took the screen

event.description: Sent when a modal, full-screen overlay on a layer below the tray (e.g. the firing-alarm or startup overlay) maps over the scene or is gone again. active is 1 while such an overlay is covering the screen, 0 once it clears. The tray retracts on active=1 so it does not sit on top of a firing alarm. Generic: any full-screen preempting overlay drives this, not a specific feature. Edge-driven: emitted on change, not replayed on bind.

arg.name: active
arg.summary: 1 = a modal overlay is covering the screen, 0 = clear
